config.title: Next.js App Router Fundamentals

intro.title: Next.js App Router Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page web application using Next.js App Router to understand how routing works in modern React frameworks. You'll learn the core concept of file-based routing, where the structure of your project's files automatically determines the URLs of your application. The main technologies involved are Next.js, React components, and special files like page.js and layout.js. By the end, you'll have a working app with multiple pages and a shared layout, all set up through the App Router's intuitive conventions.
intro.usecase: The Next.js App Router is the foundation for building modern web applications with structured navigation and optimized performance. You'll use it to create e-commerce sites where product pages, shopping carts, and checkout flows are organized in clear routes, or dashboards where different sections like analytics, user management, and settings are separated into logical paths. This pattern appears in applications like project management tools where tasks, teams, and reports each have dedicated routes, or content platforms where articles, user profiles, and search results are efficiently organized. Mastering the App Router helps you build maintainable applications with proper separation of concerns and optimized loading strategies.

objectives: Construct a new Next.js application using the App Router structure
Configure dynamic routes with parameters in the App Router
Implement page components with server-side rendering in the App Router
Integrate client-side interactivity within App Router components
Manipulate layout hierarchies using nested layouts in the App Router
Initialize data fetching within App Router components using server actions
Render dynamic metadata for SEO optimization in App Router pages

steps.title: Import Vue and createApp
steps.instruction: Import Vue and createApp from 'vue' to set up the foundation for your Vue application.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Vue and createApp from the 'vue' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing core Vue functionality
import { createApp } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have imported the necessary Vue APIs to start building your application.
successCriteria: Vue and createApp are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and createApp from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both Vue and createApp from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named App with a template and setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a component object with template and setup properties. The template can be a simple string for now, and setup should return an empty object.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and createApp here

// Create the App component below
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined with template and setup properties, ready to be used as the root component.
successCriteria: App component is created with template and setup properties, and setup returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your App component has both template and setup properties, and setup returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a component object with template and setup properties.

steps.title: Initialize reactive data with ref
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, import ref from 'vue' and initialize a reactive count variable with an initial value of 0.
steps.hint: Use the ref function from Vue to create reactive state. The import statement should be added at the top, and the ref initialization should be inside the component's setup function or script setup.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have access to a reactive count variable that can be used to track state changes.
successCriteria: ref is imported from 'vue' and a count variable is initialized with ref(0) inside the component's setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've both imported ref from 'vue' AND initialized a count variable with ref(0) inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: import ref from 'vue' and create a reactive count variable with an initial value of 0 inside the component's setup function.

steps.title: Define increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named increment that increases the count value by 1.
steps.hint: Create a regular JavaScript function that modifies the reactive count variable you initialized earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an increment function that can modify the reactive count state.
successCriteria: The increment function is defined inside setup and increases the count value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly increases the count value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment function isn't defined correctly. Check that it's inside setup and modifies the count value.

steps.title: Add template structure with main container
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's template, add a main div container with a heading that says 'Welcome to Next.js App Router'.
steps.hint: Add a <div> element inside the existing template, then place an <h2> element inside that div with the specified text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will have a main container with a welcome heading below the main title.
successCriteria: A <div> container with an <h2> element containing 'Welcome to Next.js App Router' is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some structure, but make sure to include both the <div> container and the <h2> with the exact text 'Welcome to Next.js App Router'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is incomplete. Add a <div> container with an <h2> element containing 'Welcome to Next.js App Router'.

steps.title: Display reactive count in template
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a paragraph element that displays the current count value using template interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output reactive data in Vue templates. The count variable should be referenced inside the braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current count value (initially 0) in a paragraph element.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template with {{ count }} interpolation that displays the reactive count value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using double curly braces {{ }} to display the count variable in the paragraph.
steps.feedbackWrong: The count value isn't being displayed. Check that you've added a paragraph element with {{ count }} inside the template.

steps.title: Add button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template that calls the increment function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the v-on directive (or @ shorthand) to bind the button's click event to the increment function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears below the count paragraph that increments the count when clicked.
successCriteria: The template contains a button element with a click event bound to the increment function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure its click event is properly bound to the increment function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or its click handler is missing. Add a button element with @click="increment".

steps.title: Mount the App to DOM
steps.instruction: At the bottom of your code, call createApp with your App component and mount it to the DOM element with id 'app'.
steps.hint: Use createApp(App).mount('#app') to mount your Vue application.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Vue application will be mounted to the DOM and ready to render.
successCriteria: The createApp function is called with App and mounted to '#app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling createApp with your App component and mounting it to '#app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mounting step is missing or incorrect. You need to call createApp(App).mount('#app') to mount your application.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering with v-if
steps.instruction: In the template, add a paragraph that shows only when the count is greater than 0 using v-if.
steps.hint: Use v-if directive with a condition that checks if count is greater than 0. Remember to use the reactive count value in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional rendering with v-if

Count is positive
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element that conditionally renders when count > 0.
successCriteria: Template contains a paragraph with v-if directive that checks if count > 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using v-if with the correct condition (count > 0) and the paragraph is properly placed in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional paragraph isn't quite right. Check that you're using v-if with the condition count > 0 and that the paragraph is inside the template.

steps.title: Add list rendering with v-for
steps.instruction: Create a reactive array of items in your setup function and display them as a list using v-for in your template.
steps.hint: Use ref to create a reactive array, then use v-for in your template to iterate over the array and render list items.
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will display a list of items below the button, demonstrating Vue's v-for directive for dynamic list rendering.
successCriteria: A reactive array is created with ref in setup, and the template includes a v-for directive that renders list items from the array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a reactive array with ref in setup and used v-for in the template to iterate over it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list rendering isn't working yet. Check that you've created a reactive array in setup and used v-for in your template to display the items.
